subject: Information Theory
title: Network Coding
description: A short lesson to help you apply Network Coding.

hook.text: Instead of just forwarding packets, what if routers combined them? Network coding mixes data for higher throughput.

buildup.text: In a butterfly network, two flows cross at one node. Separately: bottleneck. Combined with XOR: problem solved.

discovery.text: Network coding can achieve the max-flow bound that simple routing cannot. Mixing packets unlocks hidden capacity.

twist.text: The idea sounds counterintuitive: how can mixing information help? Because receivers can decode using other packets.

climax.text: Network coding bridges information theory and network engineering, showing that processing at nodes beats pure routing.

punchline.text: Mix packets at routers. Decode at endpoints. More throughput.

quiz.question: How does network coding increase throughput?
options: By combining packets at intermediate nodes for efficient decoding
